changes.before: Medical Device Network reports, from the company's announcement, that Medical Microinstruments (MMI) raised $125 million in an oversubscribed Series D round (a late-stage private funding round) led by existing investor BioStar Capital, with Angelini Ventures and S3 Ventures joining. The money will expand sales of MMI's Symani robot, which steadies a surgeon's hands for very small operations on blood vessels and nerves, and pay for studies including REMIND, which is testing only whether Symani is safe for microsurgery on neck lymph nodes in Alzheimer's patients; Mark Toland, chief executive of MMI, says the aim is "large-scale deployment".
changes.after: Medical Device Network reports, from the company's announcement, that Medical Microinstruments (MMI) raised $125 million in an oversubscribed Series D round (a late-stage private funding round) led by existing investor BioStar Capital, with Angelini Ventures and S3 Ventures joining. changes.reason: Company plan attributed to MMI; 'steadies a surgeon's hands' replaced by what the facts say the robot does (very small, precise movements).
